question: If two interior angles on the same side of a transversal intersecting two parallel lines are in the ratio 2 : 3, then the greater of the two angles is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **consecutive interior angles** between parallel lines is 180°.

Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 = 5 units.

5 units → 180°

1 unit → 180° ÷ 5 = 36°

Greater angle = 3 units = 3 × 36° = 108°.

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **interior angles** on the same side = 2 : 3.

**Formula Used:**

When two **parallel lines** are cut by a **transversal**, the sum of the interior angles on the same side is always 180° (supplementary angles).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f76d37fca03371db8985b1bcfd7db33b169fa187b2e1026a6ec36cb432856002.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two interior angles be 2x and 3x.

⇒ According to the property of **parallel lines**:

⇒ 2x + 3x = 180°

⇒ 5x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 5

⇒ x = 36°

⇒ Smaller angle = 2x = 2 × 36° = 72°

⇒ Greater angle = 3x = 3 × 36° = 108°

**∴ The correct answer is 108°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Interior Angles

These are the pairs of angles on one side of the transversal and between the two lines. If the lines are parallel, they are **supplementary** (sum = 180°).

Alternate Interior Angles

When a transversal intersects two parallel lines, the **alternate interior angles** are equal in measure.

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. If the lines are parallel, these angles are **equal**.</p
